SECURITY_EMAIL:
|
Please include:
- A description of the issue and its impact - Steps to reproduce, or a proof of concept - The affected endpoint, file or version (commit hash if possible) - Whether any real customer data or credentials were involved
## What to expect
| Step | Target time | |---|---| | Acknowledgement | within **3 business days** | | Initial assessment | within **7 business days** | | Fix or mitigation plan | depends on severity, shared in the assessment |
We keep you informed throughout and credit you on request once the issue is fixed.
## Scope
| In scope | Out of scope | |---|---| | Tenant isolation failures (one tenant reading or affecting another) | Issues that need physical access or a compromised device | | API key handling, authentication or authorization bypass | Denial of service through unrealistic request volumes | | Prompt injection through contract content that changes results or leaks data | Automated scanner output without a demonstrated impact | | Secrets exposure, injection flaws, insecure defaults | Social engineering |
## Good-faith research
Test only against your own deployment or data. Do not access, modify or exfiltrate data that is not yours, and do not test third-party services. We will not pursue action against researchers who follow this policy.
> [!NOTE] > Never include real contracts, credentials or customer data in a report. Use redacted or synthetic samples.
## Our security approach
- AWS access is designed to be **read-only**. - Strict **tenant isolation** and role-based access on every endpoint. - API keys are stored **hashed** and shown once. - Contract text is treated as **untrusted input**, with injection tests in CI.
## Supported versions
The project is in active development. Only the latest commit on `main` receives security fixes.
